page: Microsoft Azure L4as_v4 is a memory-optimized virtual machine powered by the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. It features an AMD EPYC 9V74 processor with an x86_64 architecture, operating at a clock speed of 3.7 GHz. The configuration includes 4 dedicated vCPUs derived from 2 physical cores with multithreading enabled. The system is equipped with 32.0 GB of RAM, providing a high memory-to-core ratio of 8.0 GB per core. For local storage, it bundles a 960 GB NVMe SSD, and it is Premium Storage capable.

Performance benchmarks indicate strong single-core capabilities, with stress-ng single-core CPU performance and Geekbench single-core scores placing in the top 25%. However, multi-core performance and memory bandwidth present some tradeoffs. While multi-core CPU performance and write bandwidth are average, read-only memory bandwidth for both small and large blocks falls into the bottom 25%. Similarly, database operations and software compilation benchmarks show weaker relative performance, though Redis SET operations remain average at 5.97 million operations per second.

Given its hardware profile, the L4as_v4 offers qualitative cost efficiency for workloads requiring a dense memory footprint and fast local NVMe storage without needing massive multi-core compute. The combination of high single-core performance and 32.0 GB of RAM makes it suitable for memory-intensive tasks, caching layers, and moderate database workloads, though it is less optimal for highly parallelized multi-threaded processing or memory-read-heavy applications.
